## Introduction

Here are the extremely brief reviews of data analysis and visualization related books that I occasionally post on [Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/jdonland.bsky.social).

### _The Theory That Would Not Die_ (McGrayne, 2011)

Brings its heroes and villains to life with charming short biographies, but mangles the statistical ideas. 

"Fisher considered a hypothesis significant if it was unlikely to have occurred by chance"? Hypotheses don't "occur" at all!

### References

- [_The Theory That Would Not Die: How Bayes' Rule Cracked the Enigma Code, Hunted Down Russian Submarines, & Emerged Triumphant from Two Centuries of Controversy_](https://www.google.ca/books/edition/The_Theory_That_Would_Not_Die/_Kx5xVGuLRIC)
